newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end lower on state selloff plan.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end lower on state selloff plan.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed sharply lower on Thursday with investors fearing a plan to accelerate a selldown of shares in state firm was a deliberate bid to cool off the market, brokers said.

Investors largely ignored Wall Street's sharp overnight rise as well as news that Beijing had approved six Taiwan shipping firms to sail directly across the Taiwan strait for the first time since 1949, brokers said.
The weighted index stayed even for most of the session but fell in late trade to end 122.68 points or 1.42 percent lower at 8,492.10. Turnover was a heavy T$149 billion.
Taiwan's provincial government announced on Wednesday that it would speed up its selldown of equity in the "big three" state-run commercial banks -- First, Hua Nan and Chang Hwa.
The announcement sank the heavily weighted financial sector by 1.70 percent on Thursday, with Chang Hwa, First Bank and Hua Nan tumbling T$1, T$4 and T$2.50 respectively to T$110.50, T$110 and T$101.
"The sell-off is not significant by itself, but investors interpreted it as part of a government effort to cool the market," said United Securities analyst Lin Long-hsien.

Before Thursday Taiwan's market, buoyed by expectations of a gathering economic recovery, had risen 25 percent in 1997 alone. But in recent sessions the index has stagnated, encountering staunch resistance at its current six-year high levels.
Losses were spread across all sectors. Plastics dropped 1.90 percent, textiles fell 0.93 percent and even electronics, widely seen as having the best fundamentals, eased 0.81 percent.

Investors all but ignored Wall Street's big rises on Tuesday and Wednesday as well as a potential political breakthrough in which communist China said six shippers from Nationalist rival Taiwan could sail direct Taiwan-China routes.
